newsitem.title: USA: Lexington, S.C. mayor seeks rainy day fund boost.
newsitem.headline: Lexington, S.C. mayor seeks rainy day fund boost.

text.p: Mayor Pam Miller has proposed that Lexington, S.C., boost its rainy day fund by setting aside five percent of general fund revenues instead of the current one percent, the Herald Leader reported Wednesday.

Miller suggested that while the economy is strong, the city should put four percent of general fund revenues, or about $5.7 million of the current year's budget, into a contingency fund to cover major emergencies.
She urged that an additional one percent, or $1.5 million, be put into a separate contingency fund to meet unexpected year-to-year spending demands or make budget adjustments.

Up to now the city has maintained a budgeted reserve of only about $1.5 million. Miller said that left the city in dire straits in 1992 when a revenue slowdown related to the recession reduced the city's reserves to $12,000.
